description: Backend sky-map chatbot end to end: generated DTOs + path, per-constellation RA/Dec centers (model fields, generated JSON table, seeder back-fill), AstronomyService (JD/LST port, inverse alt/az, rise solver, four-state classifier, compass map), GroqService phrasing entry point, SkyChatService (validation + fuzzy name resolution + orchestration + dynamic system prompt), SkyChatController, security permit rule, exception + two 400 handler branches, and the backend unit/integration tests. One coherent backend unit — the controller depends on the service, which depends on the astronomy math and the generated DTOs; it must build and test together. Depends on nothing else; FEAT-002 (frontend) depends on this feature's /skymap/chat contract. Grounded in design.md sections 1-8 and verified against the actual source listed in context.json.
steps: In src/main/resources/openapi.yaml add the /skymap/chat path (operationId chatWithSky, tag SkyMap, requestBody SkyChatRequest required, 200 -> SkyChatResponse) and three component schemas per design.md section 2: SkyChatRequest (messages: array of existing #/components/schemas/ChatMessage, required; latitude/longitude: number double, required; time: string format date-time, optional), SkyChatResponse (reply: string; visibility: $ref VisibilityFacts, nullable/optional), VisibilityFacts (constellation, abbreviation, state, compass, riseCompass: string; altitudeDeg, azimuthDeg, nextRiseInHours: number double; nextRiseUtc: string format date-time). Reuse the existing ChatMessage schema; do NOT hand-write DTO classes.
Add `private Double centerRa;` and `private Double centerDec;` (nullable, Lombok @Getter/@Setter like the rest) to src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/model/Constellation.java.

Generate src/main/resources/constellation-centers.json with the design.md Appendix script: for each of the 88 abbreviations in celestia_fe/public/data/data/constellations.json, centroid ONLY the line-member HIPs (membersHips = unique(flatten(con.lines)), resolved via the HIP index from celestia_fe/public/data/data/stars_full.json), weight w = max(0.1, 6 - mag), avgRa = atan2(sum sin(ra)*w, sum cos(ra)*w) normalized to [0,360), avgDec = sum(dec*w)/sum(w); skip any constellation whose line members resolve to <2 catalog stars; round to 2dp. Output a JSON object keyed by abbreviation: { "And": {"ra":9.27,"dec":37.74}, ... }. Verify the sample anchors And 9.27/37.74, Ori 81.92/4.36, Cru 188.65/-59.31 before saving.

Restructure src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/config/ConstellationSeeder.run per design.md section 1: load constellation-centers.json into a Map<String,double[]> keyed by abbreviation FIRST (before any guard); if constellationRepository.count()==0 do the existing fresh seed from constellations.json, set centerRa/centerDec on each from the centers map by abbreviation, saveAll, and return; else (already seeded) stream existing constellations, set centerRa/centerDec from the map on every doc whose centerRa is null, collect the mutated subset and saveAll(changed) once. Seeder is the single writer of these fields; back-fill is idempotent.

Create src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/service/AstronomyService.java as a stateless @Service with instance methods: toJD(OffsetDateTime/Instant at UTC) and getLST(jd, lon) ported verbatim from astronomy.js (both degrees, Math.floor to match JS integer flooring); altAz(ra,dec,lst,lat) returning alt and az with azimuth measured North-through-East (H=LST-RA; sin(alt)=sin(lat)sin(dec)+cos(lat)cos(dec)cos(H), alt=asin(clamp)); az=atan2(-sin(H)cos(dec), cos(lat)sin(dec)-sin(lat)cos(dec)cos(H)) then (deg+360)%360); the rise-time solver (x=-tan(lat)tan(dec): x>1 never rises, x<-1 circumpolar, else H0=acos(x), deltaLstDeg=((RA-H0)-LST+360)%360, deltaHours=deltaLstDeg/15*(1/1.0027379), nextRiseUtc=now+deltaHours, then +/- minutes refinement using altAz; degraded fallback emits nextRiseInHours from analytic deltaHours (rounded, strictly >0) and omits nextRiseUtc); the four-state classifier in the design.md section 3.6 order using named constants HORIZON_BAND_DEG=3.0 and VISIBLE_MIN_DEG=3.0 (alt>VISIBLE_MIN -> VISIBLE; |alt|<=HORIZON_BAND -> AT_HORIZON; else x>1 -> NEVER_VISIBLE else BELOW_RISES); and the 8-point compass COMPASS[(int)Math.round(az/45.0)%8] = [N,NE,E,SE,S,SW,W,NW]. Expose a small record/struct of visibility facts (state, altitudeDeg, azimuthDeg, compass, nextRiseUtc, nextRiseInHours, riseCompass) for SkyChatService to map into the generated VisibilityFacts.

In src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/service/GroqService.java expose a public phrasing entry point: either make the private 2-arg chat(List<Map<String,String>> messages, String systemPrompt) public, or add public String chatRaw(List<Map<String,String>> messages, String systemPrompt) wrapping it in the same try/catch that returns the friendly fallback string used by the existing public chat(constellationName, history). Do not change the existing public chat behavior.
Add src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/exception/InvalidSkyChatRequestException.java (runtime exception, same style as ConstellationNotFound).

In src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/exception/GlobalExceptionHandler.java add two @ExceptionHandler branches, mirroring the existing invalidCredentialsException branch, each returning new ErrorMessage(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST.value(), e.getMessage()) with @ResponseStatus(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST): one for InvalidSkyChatRequestException, one for org.springframework.http.converter.HttpMessageNotReadableException (so a malformed time or JSON body returns 400 instead of falling through to the Exception->500 handler).

Create src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/service/SkyChatService.java (@Service, constructor-injected ConstellationRepository, AstronomyService, GroqService): validate the request (latitude in [-90,90], longitude in [-180,180], non-empty messages; throw InvalidSkyChatRequestException otherwise); resolve the constellation from the latest user message via normalize -> direct name/abbreviation/alias maps (built once from the seeded constellations plus a small checked-in alias Map<String,String> big dipper/plough->UMa, little dipper->UMi, scorpius/scorpio->Sco, the hunter->Ori) -> whole-word token scan -> local Levenshtein fallback (FUZZY_MAX_DISTANCE=2, matched token length >=4); on a resolved constellation with non-null centerRa/centerDec call AstronomyService to compute facts and build the FACTS system prompt per design.md section 5 (NEVER_VISIBLE: say never rises, give no direction; BELOW_RISES: always include next_rise_in_hours + rise_compass, include next_rise_utc when present); otherwise (no match, or null centers) build the general astronomy-guide system prompt and omit visibility; map request.getMessages() into List<Map<String,String>> exactly as ConstellationService.chat does and pass the full transcript + system prompt to the GroqService entry point from the step above; return a generated SkyChatResponse with reply and the mapped VisibilityFacts (or null). Fuzzy/alias thresholds and the alias table are named constants.

Add src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/controller/SkyChatController.java: @RestController @RequestMapping("/skymap"), POST /chat method chatWithSky(@RequestBody SkyChatRequest) -> SkyChatResponse delegating to SkyChatService, mirroring ConstellationController.
In src/main/java/org/celestia/backend/config/SecurityConfig.java add .requestMatchers("/skymap/**").permitAll() next to the existing .requestMatchers("/constellations/**").permitAll() line.

Add src/test/java/org/celestia/backend/service/AstronomyServiceTest.java (pure unit, lat 44.4 / LST 100 where applicable): Dec=+90 -> alt~=44.4 (±0.01) & az~=0; RA==LST & Dec=10 -> az~=180 & alt~=55.6; RA==LST & Dec==lat -> alt~=90; Crux dec~=-59.31 from lat 44.4 -> NEVER_VISIBLE; a near-equatorial constellation currently below the horizon with x<=1 -> BELOW_RISES with nextRiseUtc a future instant within ~24h, nextRiseInHours in (0,24], valid 8-point riseCompass; compass bins 0->N,90->E,180->S,270->W,135->SE,350->N; toJD/getLST equal a hard-coded frontend-computed value for a fixed sample date.

Add src/test/java/org/celestia/backend/service/SkyChatServiceTest.java (unit, stubbed ConstellationRepository returning seeded constellations with centers, mocked GroqService): 'where is the big dipper' -> UMa, 'orioon' (typo) -> Ori via fuzzy, 'ori' -> Ori, gibberish -> no match / null visibility.

Add src/test/java/org/celestia/backend/controller/SkyChatIntegrationTest.java (@WebMvcTest(SkyChatController.class) excluding SecurityAutoConfiguration + SecurityFilterAutoConfiguration, MockMvc, @MockBean SkyChatService, mirroring AuthControllerTest): POST /skymap/chat with lat/lon/messages returns 200 and the mocked VisibilityFacts; missing latitude -> 400; empty messages -> 400.

`./mvnw -q -Dtest=AstronomyServiceTest,SkyChatServiceTest,SkyChatIntegrationTest test` from app/Celestia/celestia_be passes all new tests, including the four design test anchors (Dec=+90 -> alt~=lat & az~=0; RA==LST on meridian -> az~=180; Crux from lat 44.4 -> NEVER_VISIBLE/state 4; a below-but-rising constellation -> BELOW_RISES/state 3 with a plausible future rise time).
constellation-centers.json exists with ~88 keyed entries and the sample anchors (And, Ori, Cru) match the design table within rounding.
No change to existing sky-map rendering code; application.properties and mvnw are not in the diff; no secret value appears in the diff.

findings:
Implemented and verified. `./mvnw -q -DskipTests package` succeeds and generates org.celestia.generated.model.SkyChatRequest, SkyChatResponse, VisibilityFacts. The three test classes pass (7 + 4 + 3 = 14 tests, 0 failures). NOTE for the build: the active system JDK is 27 but Lombok 1.18.34 only supports up to JDK 21; builds/tests MUST run with JAVA_HOME pointing at the installed JDK 21 (/Users/dariacraciun/Library/Java/JavaVirtualMachines/ms-21.0.12.1/Contents/Home), otherwise the compiler fails with 'java.lang.ExceptionInInitializerError: com.sun.tools.javac.code.TypeTag :: UNKNOWN'. This is an environment issue, not a code issue; the project targets Java 21.

CONTRACT for FEAT-002 (frontend) and the integration step:

Endpoint: POST /skymap/chat (permitted anonymously via SecurityConfig .requestMatchers("/skymap/**").permitAll()).

Request body = generated SkyChatRequest JSON: { messages: [{role, content}, ...] (required, non-empty, last user message is read for the constellation), latitude: number (required, [-90,90]), longitude: number (required, [-180,180]), time: ISO-8601 date-time string (optional; omitted => server uses now UTC). A malformed `time`/body => 400 (HttpMessageNotReadableException handler). Out-of-range lat/lon or empty messages => 400 (InvalidSkyChatRequestException handler). Both 400s return the existing ErrorMessage shape { status, message }.

Response body = generated SkyChatResponse JSON: { reply: string, visibility: VisibilityFacts | null }. visibility is null for general/unresolved questions or when the resolved constellation has null centers.

VisibilityFacts (generated DTO) exact field names (camelCase JSON): constellation (string, full IAU name), abbreviation (string, 3-letter), state (string: one of VISIBLE | AT_HORIZON | BELOW_RISES | NEVER_VISIBLE), altitudeDeg (number), azimuthDeg (number), compass (string, 8-point N/NE/E/SE/S/SW/W/NW). Rise fields present ONLY when state == BELOW_RISES: nextRiseUtc (ISO-8601 date-time, a real ...Z UTC instant; may be absent in the degraded refinement fallback), nextRiseInHours (number, always present for BELOW_RISES, strictly > 0), riseCompass (string, 8-point). For NEVER_VISIBLE no rise fields and the LLM is instructed to give no direction. Frontend should format nextRiseUtc with new Date(nextRiseUtc).toLocaleString() in the browser's own zone (backend never guesses a civil offset); the reply text already phrases the 'in about N hours' delta.

Name resolution: alias table (big dipper/plough->UMa, little dipper->UMi, scorpius/scorpio->Sco, the hunter->Ori), direct name/abbreviation lookup, whole-word token scan, then local Levenshtein fuzzy (max distance 2, token length >= 4). centerRa/centerDec live on the Constellation document, written only by ConstellationSeeder (fresh-seed or idempotent null back-fill) from constellation-centers.json (88 keyed entries).
